notes:
- sitrep goes quiet within seconds of launch on a large corpus. With about
  10,000 documents the catch-up scan after launch held a full processor core
  for 71 minutes; the same scan now takes 7 seconds. The counts beside the
  list answer in 0.2 seconds where they took 6.7.

- Search finds a document by its file name. Every word you type can match
  anywhere in the path, in any order, and a file whose name holds them all
  is listed first, with the words marked in its title and file name.

- The copy button on the reader's path has a menu: copy the full or relative
  path, copy the file itself (paste it into Finder, Slack or Mail), copy its
  markdown, or show it in Finder. One click on the icon still copies the full
  path.

- Cmd+O opens relative paths. `docs/plan.md` resolves against the document
  you are reading, its project, then any indexed file whose path ends that
  way; when several do, the dialog lists them.

- Each folder in the reader's path is a link that lists every document in
  that folder. The folder chip it leaves in the list header shows it in
  Finder, ignores it, or tags it. A tag is kept by sitrep, never written into
  your files, covers every document under the folder, and gets its own
  section in the Filter menu.

- A repository cloned into a workspace shows up while sitrep is running.
  `git clone` creates the folder seconds before it writes the files, and the
  watcher looked only once, when the folder appeared, so a clone stayed
  invisible until the next restart. The watcher now looks again whenever
  anything moves inside a new folder during its first minutes.

- Folders named `adr` are indexed without asking in new workspaces, next to
  `docs`. Existing configs keep their own list; add `**/adr/**` to Settings >
  Corpus > Auto-include globs to get the same.
